result.title: Emergent Sparsity: How Many Effective Variables Survive Coarse-Graining in AlphaEarth Embeddings?
result.comment: Camera-ready version of a paper accepted at the 2nd Workshop on Advances in Representation Learning for Earth Observation (REO), NeurIPS 2026. 20 pages, 15 figures
result.summary: AlphaEarth encodes each 10 m land pixel as a 64-component vector intended to support diverse global mapping tasks. Yet many scientific applications work at coarser spatial supports, for which fewer than 64 effective variables may suffice. We ask whether these vectors can be reorganized into ranked global nonlinear coordinates, how many suffice at a chosen reconstruction accuracy, and whether that number decreases with spatial scale. We thus describe effective dimension as a two-control surface over tolerance and spatial scale, rather than one intrinsic number. At each scale, a $β$-VAE scan with a common architecture produces a rank--distortion envelope, giving the smallest retained count achieved within the scanned family at each reconstruction tolerance. At 3% validation tolerance, this number falls from 24 to 7 when the scale is increased from 10 m to 78.9 km, whereas the corresponding PCA rank falls only from 46 to 38. Repeating the analysis on unit-norm targets preserves this trend.

AI.brief_summary: 论文以 AlphaEarth 的 64 维地表像元嵌入为对象，用统一架构的 β-VAE 扫描得到 rank–distortion 包络，考察在指定重建容差下保留下来的有效变量数如何随空间尺度粗粒化而下降（3% 容差时由 24 降至 7，而 PCA 秩仅由 46 降至 38）。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「容差—尺度」二维有效维度刻画与表示几何相关，可能为核查 latent 推理状态中视觉信息随压缩与粒度变化的坍缩提供度量思路；但对象是遥感嵌入而非 VLM 推理，联系仅为概念类比，需较多核查。
